nodes.description: As-left torque switch setting on 3-FCV-001-0055 resulted in negative margin; MOV close circuit effectively on torque switch control instead of limit switch control.

nodes.display_name: Failure to identify valve susceptibility during extent-of-condition review
nodes.description: SQN NCV CR 1603101 extent-of-condition review at BFN in 2020 failed to identify 3-FCV-001-0055 as susceptible because the torque switch and bypass limit switch were not identified in the MOV Program Database.

nodes.display_name: PCIV may not fully close/seal under design basis differential pressure
nodes.description: If differential pressure across the valve was great enough to cause the torque switch to open prior to the limit switch opening, the valve might not fully close or seal hard enough to prevent seat leakage.

chain: legacy close-control wiring scheme (torque switch control instead of limit switch) [cause TBD] -> not identified during 2020 SQN NCV extent-of-condition review -> PCIV 3-FCV-001-0055 may not fully close/seal under DBA differential pressure -> PCIV inoperable, TS 3.6.1.3/3.0.4 violations [backup: redundant outboard PCIV 3-FCV-001-0056 remained operable]
notes: Official cause_code/category not provided in FORM-366 FIELDS (TBD/provisional) despite narrative describing a clear human-performance/design legacy issue; per rules the official code governs and is copied verbatim. Previous similar event is at a different plant (Sequoyah), captured as SIMILAR_TO stub LER per rule 9, using the CR number as the closest available identifier since no LER number was given for the referenced NCV. 3-FCV-001-0056 modeled as a Component (not System) since it is the redundant valve, not a new system; BACKED_UP_BY edge from Consequence to Component reflects the redundant valve backup. HPCI/RCIC systems mentioned only as reasons for periodic valve openings (maintenance context), not as failure-chain participants or as operable backups performing the isolation function -- retained as System nodes per INVOLVES since the event narrative ties their maintenance activities directly to the valve's open/closed history relevant to the single-point-vulnerability analysis.
